_note: THE CHARACTER SLOT. scripts/knight.gd reads this and nothing else about who the occupant is. `clips` maps the ROLES the scene drives to whatever the GLB calls them; `clips_armed` is the SECOND set, used whenever every piece in `armed_when_pieces` is equipped. `forward_axis` is the direction the MODEL faces in its own space -- MEASURED from the walk clip's stance foot. Speeds come from each clip's OWN stride so the feet do not slide, and they are quoted at `speed_measured_at_scale`: knight.gd rescales them to whatever figure scale is live, because a smaller man takes smaller steps.

Measured: the walk clip's stance-foot floor is 6.8 mm/frame median at 1.25178 and 11.4 mm at 1.10 (24 of 39 pairs under 10 mm against 13 of 39). Roughly 40% of what was recorded as the walk clip's own floor was this. knight.gd now scales both speeds by _figure_scale / speed_measured_at_scale.
_armed_speed_note: MEASURED, tools/probe_stride_armed.gd (in-place clips) and tools/probe_root.gd (travelling ones). walk_armed is IN PLACE: 42 frames / 1.7500 s for a 2.0625 m world stride = 118.6 px/s by the all-frames stance median and 115.4 by the contact-filtered one (6 pairs) -- 2.8% apart, which is the agreement that makes either usable. The unarmed 201.7 would slide his feet 70%. run_armed and strafe_L_armed carry ROOT MOTION and state their own speeds once de-rooted (4.337 m/s and 0.931 m/s), so no number for them is stored here: knight.gd reads the speed off the track it removed, which cannot go stale.
_walk_armed_angle_finding: walk_armed's travel is +9.6 deg off the model's +Z, contact-filtered (walk's is +0.0). An EARLIER figure of 24.3 deg in this file was my own instrument: the all-frames median takes the lower foot on every frame, and on a clip that is airborne or swinging for most of them that is a SWINGING foot. Not compensated in the scene -- 9.6 deg is small and a weight-dependent yaw offset would put a rotation into the walk-run transitions.

arm_layer_armed._over: idle, walk and run only -- it sits BELOW the block and the three one-shots in the tree, so a slash, chop, bash or block owns the left arm outright while it is running.
arm_layer_armed._source: Meshy 138 Block1, left-arm chain at 0.70 weight, already baked into the clip; the scene applies it at weight 1.0 and does not re-scale it.

_block_note: Block is a HOLD, so it is a Blend2 this script drives rather than an AnimationNodeOneShot, which cannot be held for as long as a key is down. Full body, and it roots him. WHILE BLOCKING: an input toward his strafe side side-steps at strafe_L_armed's own 93.7 px/s with his facing HELD; any other input TURNS him on the spot; he never runs. There is one strafe clip and it goes one way -- Godot has no skeleton mirroring for an AnimationTree and a mirrored body would put the shield on the wrong arm -- so right-hand input turns instead of side-stepping.

transitions._loco_w_tau_note: 0 = OFF. Slewing the run weight at 0.10 s was tried and REJECTED on its own numbers: it improved the run stop (813.9 -> 301.2 mm worst) and made the crossover worse (294.6 -> 415.1 mm worst, median 41.1 -> 52.2), which is the documented cost of lagging w appearing exactly where the comment says it would. The mechanism is kept because it is the only dial that separates pose response from body response, and one number turns it on.
transitions._accel_tau_note: 0.08 -> 0.22 for the armed set. The armed gait span is narrow (94 -> 344 px/s against the unarmed 202 -> 648), so the same speed ramp moves the blend weight much further per frame, and walk_armed and run_armed are far less alike than walk and run. w was jumping 0 -> 0.602 in ONE frame. Accel only; the decel constants and therefore the stop times are untouched.

_root_motion_finding: FOUR CLIPS TRAVEL and the rest are in place -- Hips net horizontal displacement, tools/probe_root.gd: run_armed 8.6617 m (4.337 m/s), strafe_L_armed 1.8591 m (0.931 m/s), idle_armed 0.8994 m (0.184 m/s) and attack_chop 0.7519 m (0.123 m/s); walk, run, walk_armed, run_armed_locked, block and shield_bash are all under 9 mm. The first two are known; THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT FLAGGED ANYWHERE -- an idle that walks 0.90 m over its loop would have slid him sideways while standing still, and the chop lunges 0.75 m. knight.gd._deroot_all converts all four to in-place plus a speed at load, detected by measurement rather than by a list, so a re-export that fixes one cannot leave a stale entry behind.
_armed_walk_stop_unmeasurable: The armed walk stop reports 0 planted frames of 11, so there is NO number for it -- not 0 mm. walk_armed never produces a frame PAIR where the same foot is within 3 cm of its lowest on both frames with its height unchanged, at 24 fps. Reported as unmeasurable rather than as zero.
_clip_px_s_note: FALLBACK ONLY. knight.gd reads locomotion speeds from the shipped export manifest's locomotion_in_place block (speed_m_s, the FOOT-LOCK speed on the clip's own keys since T12_10). This table is canvas px/s AT THE REFERENCE SCALE (speed_measured_at_scale), like walk_px_s and run_px_s: the strafes and run_armed here are the manifest's m/s x PPM x the reference, so both paths drive the same speed (tools/manifest_speed_patch.py fixed the manifest path, which had used PPM alone and driven every manifest speed at 0.799). walk_armed is in place at source and has no speed of its own: 115.1 is this scene's contact-filtered stance rate, kept.
_strafe_dirs_note: From the export manifest's own frame -- his_right is -X, so his left is +X -- rather than from the clips' measured net travel. The measured headings agree (+98.1 deg off +Z for L, -137.8 for R, both resolving to the right side) but a name and an axis convention are firmer than a net direction taken from 6 contact pairs.
_armed_run_restored: run_armed is BACK as the armed run: the export trimmed it to one gait cycle, which was the exact objection. It had held about four cycles in 2.5 s and the sync group's premise is one cycle per clip; the crossover worst frame was 316.2 mm against run_armed_locked's 30.4 mm. Re-measured after the trim -- see the commit.
_loop_note: strafe_l / strafe_r added 2026-09-29. They are locomotion cycles and were not looped, and the strf Blend2 has sync on, which ADVANCES an input even at zero weight -- so by the time he first side-stepped, the strafe clip had run to its last frame and stayed there, and the body slid at the strafe speed over still legs (attack_lab: a_strafe parked at 2.458 s of 2.458 after 4 s of standing).

block_timing._note: Block is RAISE -> HOLD -> LOWER. knight.gd._block_marks reads where Block1's raise starts and where it peaks off the clip itself (the shield hand's last low before its highest point: 0.750 -> 1.333 s as shipped), so these are only the durations: the raise played in raise_s (x3.24 of the clip), pinned at the peak while held, reversed over lower_s on release, then the 0.12 s blend back to guard. Measured, attack_lab: full guard 0.177 s after the press (was 1.458), the raise over 4 game frames and 0.587 m of hand travel, hold drift 0.0000 m (was 0.198), back to guard 0.333 s after release.

What the lock added is in the LEGS: it held feet up to 0.845 m from where the clip puts them (2.17 s of the sequence over 0.15 m) and folded a knee up to 61 deg past the clip's own angle, at the strikes' ends and the block's start. _foot_lock_note: scripts/foot_lock.gd: at the start of a strike, a block, or their fade-outs, every foot that is not mid-stride is held where it stands by leg IK (Godot's TwoBoneIK3D) for the transition's own fade, then released over 0.2 s -- as a STEP (lift first, travel, plant) when it has more than 4 cm to go. A foot left to finish a run stride locks where it lands. false turns it off.

strike_release._note: THE RECOVERY RELEASE (T12, coordinator 2026-09-30: every strike gives the axe arm back at its swing end). A strike owns every bone; after its ACTIVE SWING -- the frames contiguous with the axe head's peak speed at >= 50% of it, the weapon gate's definition -- its follow-through drove the seated axe through his own body. From at_s[clip] (that swing's last frame, measured on the clip by attack_lab/t12/godot/tools/guard_accept.gd) the arm blends to its guard over over_s, eased, inside the one-shot; weapon_r blends to its rest (the mount). pose_for gives a clip its own guard where `pose` would not hold: the chop's post-swing crouch (axe_guard_R_chop) and the shield bash's lunge (axe_guard_R_bash), each solved against that clip's own torso (attack_lab/tools/bash_guard_solve.py) and verified 0 penetration on the mesh. guard_throughout: clips that never take the axe arm -- the shield bash, whose swing is the shield's. A clip with no at_s keeps its arm throughout. knight.gd: _apply_strike_release / _release_tick (attack_lab/tools/strike_release_patch.py).
strike_release._note_t12_11: T12_11 (the slash re-cut on nbt_attack.glb's own 30 fps keys): at_s.attack RE-DERIVED on the re-cut -- its active swing is 0.5417-0.7083 s (the gate's rule on the raw clip; the strike frame 0.5833), so the swing ends at 0.708333 (17/24), not 0.75. FROM_SWING_END: a clip listed there (clip: its own ease, s) is released from its swing-end pose HELD, eased to the guard inside the release clip, the weight a step at at_s (knight.gd _release_hold_for; attack_lab/tools/strike_hold_release_patch.py). The re-cut's follow-through drives the axe into his head and left shoulder 11 ms after its swing ends (0.719 s at a 1/96 s step; 0.05-0.17 m deep over 0.72-0.82 s with no release), faster than the eased release can take the arm out of it: released from the running clip at 0.708 over 0.08 s, 228 axe points were inside his head at 0.75 s. Held, 0 at 1/24 and at 1/96 s, for eases of 0.08, 0.12, 0.16 and 0.24 s; 0.08 was kept then; T12_11b makes every release 0.16 (below). The chop and the bash release as before.

strike_trail._note: THE STRIKE TRAIL (T12_11, knight.gd StrikeTrail; attack_lab/tools/strike_trail_patch.py): a brushed ink-and-wash stroke behind the weapon's EDGE LINE through each strike's active swing, faded out over fade_s after the swing's last frame. edge: two points in `bone`'s frame (glTF units), inner then outer (the outer carries the pen): the axe's cutting edge, beard to top horn, in weapon_r's; for the shield bash, the shield's rim diameter most ACROSS its travel (130 deg from its first axis toward its second: speed-weighted |cos| with the travel 0.20), in LeftHand's, the end that sweeps the longer path outer. window: clip seconds, the ACTIVE SWING by the weapon gate's own rule (the frames contiguous with the peak speed at >= 50% of it): the slash and the chop as the gate finds them on the raw clip (53_weapon_gate.py EDGE: attack 0.5417-0.7083, chop_overhead_92 0.4127-0.5778); the bash on the SHIELD's centre, through the tree at 1/192 s (1.0313-1.1979; the gate's bash row follows the carried axe head, not the shield that strikes). style (T12_11b, the coordinator's ruling: it must read on the snow): a TWO-TONE stroke -- a SHADE BODY in the painter's own shadow hue (0.42/0.55/0.89 linear) taken deeper, x0.55 on its lit side and x0.35 on its shade side under the scene's sun (wash_color / shade_color, sRGB), laid heavy (alpha_max 0.95, the streaks' thinnest paint 0.6, the wash full from 30% of the width in, thinning toward the tail as (1-v)^0.4), a PALE EDGE (the old warm white) over the outer 35% of its width, and the gear's ink along the rim.
strike_trail._render_priority_note: style.render_priority 126 = paint_stack.gd AFTER_POST_PRIORITY: the painted Barrow's post pass paints its pre-transparent screen copy over the whole frame at 120, so a transparent stroke drawn before it is painted out (the snowfall's rule). Harmless where there is no post pass (the lab).
strike_trail._look_t12_11b: Why two-tone, measured in the painted Barrow (attack_lab/t12/godot/tools/trail_contrast_scene.gd: the same takes with and without the trail, frame-identical, the stroke's body = where a black mask take shows at least a quarter of its paint; 2 placements, 4 ticks per strike): the old pale wash moved the snow by 0.031 median luminance (it is the snow's own value); the painter's shadow colour itself, 0.036 (0.76 against snow 0.89 at partial paint cannot reach 0.10); a deep single tone reached the snow (0.133) but sank into the rocks and scrub (0.077-0.100: its value is theirs); the two-tone keeps both -- the shade body reads on snow, the pale edge over dark ground. Chosen: snow 0.111 / 0.108, rock 0.126 / 0.129, scrub 0.111 (the placement with scrub), over him 0.208 / 0.203 (median |dL|, the two placements). Shaded snow stays low (0.05-0.06): its value is the stroke's.
